notes.title: Clawed Demo. Where we are now, a big thank you, what's next, and Co-op.
notes.content:
Hi Prehistorians!

Tim here again. It's been a few weeks since our last post, so we thought we would touch base with you all and let you know where we are at in terms of development, the co-op update for the demo and so on.
So, let's get to it!

Community Growth, Clawed demo feedback, and a huge thank you for all that this community has done.

For us, this game has been a rollercoaster - it is not a big budget production nor are we a big budget studio, yet - thanks to all of you - Clawed has a rapidly growing community, is now in the top 500 most Wishlisted games on steam, has a growing presence on Twitch, and every single day we are seeing more and more content creators stream the demo on YouTube and share it. 
Thing about this is, this is not our success as a team (we really mean this) - but all of you that chose to support our dino game. 
This community has been unexpected but in the best way possible - You are actively helping shape the game into a better experience through constructive feedback and fair critique, you took the time to play it when there are so many other games out there to try, and many of you reached out to us directly to share your experience. 
We are sitting on your shoulders, and we want everyone to know that we really appreciate the level of support and (sometimes tough) love you have sent our way.
We are under no illusion that we did this - it was all of you.

And we can't thank you enough.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45418326/a2acbc571cf900678d1ccbc9c2dfc581b48d1e50.png"]
So, now that the soppy stuff is over - what does this mean for the game?

Well, the demo has acted as a guidepost for what is working well, what needs to be improved and what isn't working well. 
Thanks to the popularity of the game so far, we are able to invest in the game a bit more, which means we can take more feedback, improve more systems and so on. Basically, it allows us to reinvest in the game so that when this game launches it is do so in a great place

- We are working on improving some of our dinosaur models, (the Meg recently had a big facelift and looks more terrifying than ever) Our Rexes have been updated too and several more are getting a glow up.

- Our Dino AI has had a complete from the ground up overhaul. You can expect more unique behaviors, new ways to deal with them, and tweaks based on player feedback. We are planning to go bit deeper into this in the next community post when we break down the Co-op demo update.

-New weapons, tools, and items. Again, not going to give this away yet, but I think you guys will be happy with some changes and new features.

- New task system to help manage and track current goals. We are working on the balance of this as we still want the game to be about exploring and solving puzzles on your own. No doubt the community will have plenty of feedback on this when it rolls out as part of the co-op update.

That sort of covers the basics. There are other parts of the game that are benefiting too such as Tourist Mode and Envara Expedition. We will have more on those after to Co-op update rolls out.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45418326/c0d705af72df2f4fe2884791b1978b2cf649d44c.png"]
Speaking of the Co-Op update, when is that happening?

To not bury to lead, in roughly two weeks. Possibly sooner but I'll say two to be safe as we don't want to disappoint you guys.
So, many of the mentioned things above will be rolled out into the demo along with the Co-op option being enabled. 
Our original plans were to just turn on Co-op for the current version of the demo and be done with it.
However, the benefits of community feedback have been so useful, we thought we'd make a bigger effort and use it to gather feedback on the improved systems as well. 
There will be a couple of new spaces to explore, new items, goals, and new dino AI.
Our next post will be a breakdown of the coming update, so stay tuned for that :)

A Quick Q&A - some of the questions we are seeing out in the community.

The demo is quite large, how big is the full game? Is this a 5 hour game?
The easiest way to answer this is - it's much bigger. The Demo allows you to explore South Main Street, an area of the park that was closed 20 years prior to the main story.
There is still the entire main park to explore. 
Basically, you have barely seen the park yet, and if you finished the demo and experienced the final tram ride, you can see the park extends far into the distance. That doesn't include the areas you can't see, such as the many tunnels, caves, underwater areas and so on.

Then there is Tourist Mode - Explore Prehistoria during its operation as a tourist. You can even buy yourself hotdogs and toys :)

Envara Expedition - Not going to share too much on this yet. But I will say it provides a completely different kind of experience and takes place on Envara island, where the dinos in our story were discovered.

All modes can be played with up to 4 players :)

Will the game be expensive?
As I said when we started, this is not a triple A game, and we won't be charging AAA prices obviously. We honestly don't know the exact price yet, but it will be fair and respectful to the gamer.
If you have bought an Indy title, then you probably know the ballpark where it will be.

Our goal is ultimately that you feel the game provides a lot of value for your money. So, we're leading with that

Is the game still coming out this year? If so, when?
Yes! We have no intention of pushing it back. We have a window in mind.
While we are still refining things like AI, animations, environments and some systems, the bulk of the work is well near completion. Our Park is getting final touches and testing, and the other modes have been in the oven for a while.

We will not be dragging out a prolonged release date. Once we think it's good to go, you'll know, and we will announce the date.


So, I think this is a good place to leave it. 
Again, thank you all for the support. We appreciate it more than you know.

If you have questions, please leave them in the comments. We try to get back quickly - sometimes we can't - but we read everything and will do our best to reply.

Have a great day everyone :)

Flatrock Team

notes.title: Demo Patch v0.15
notes.content:
Hi everyone, 

We have released a new patch for demo and have addressed some the feedback from the community.
Again, thank you for helping us improve the Clawed experience. It really is appreciated.

The details:

-The save game update bug has been fixed, however it will require a fresh start/save file to be compatible with future updates.

-Fixed Audio sliders not working correctly in the audio settings. 
-Weather Volume now has a slider in the audio settings
-A sprint Toggle option is now available under control settings (Gamepad player rejoice!)

-Adjustments have been made to global illumination in response to feedback the game is a bit too dark. Additional lights have also been added to South Main Street.  We will keep monitoring the feedback on this.
-new environment objects have been added to assist with directing players towards items/locations required for progression

-Item stack sizes have been increased to improve inventory management
-the new Flashlight now dims when reading notes (You know, allowing you to actually read them....)
-Ambient audio levels and dino noises have been raised. We are also working on more ambient improvements 
-Fixed a save bug when trying to save in the viewing towers.


We will have more updates rolling out over the next week. Here are some of the focus points:

-Dino respawning after a save will be addressed.
-A Objective list will be added next to your inventory screen
-Dino reactions to being shot will be improved.
-Dinos occasionally/briefly pausing before attacking will be addressed
-We will be adding a tranquilizer rifle to the demo for a non-lethal option
-Crouching IS being added to the game
-A Map item will be implemented for different Park Areas.

As we have already mention in the previous posts, Co-op is will be unlocked in the main menu once the work on the above has been rolled out. Won't be long!

Thats about it from us today.

Thanks to everyone for checking out the demo. We really appreciate you guys.
If you have any thoughts, let us know below or in the demo feedback discussion :)

Flatrock Games :)

notes.title: Demo Feedback Update
notes.content:
Prehistorians! Good morning!

Tim here again,

Okay, just going to quickly drop this post here to keep all you guys in the loop with your demo feedback.

First of all, though, I know this is buttering you all up, but can I just say the amount of good constructive feedback we have received has been unbelievable. 
I say the word constructive deliberately because that's exactly what this has been. In the gaming space, you can see some nasty stuff out there. Yet that has not been the bulk of our experience today. 
While a small trove of new bugs has been encountered and people have had issues with the demo, we have received so much support, words of encouragement and kindness in the last 24 hours that I had to say something.
And that is simply - Thank you. 

If this is the community we have, then we hit the jackpot.

So, onto the feedback! This is just some of our priorities and movements but not all. We are listening :)
We are a small team, but we are reading every comment. We will get back to as well, it just takes us a bit as we are working on resolving the issues and feedback.

Okay, Firstly: The Save Game Bug

As a lot of you have encountered, after our update yesterday, people returned to find their progress had reset, some gates had closed again and so on. This is a big issue and i just want to say sorry to all of you that had to restart the demo in order to progress. Its not cool. 
This got past us, because during testing we have traditionally started fresh saves for each version to test the demo from start to finish. 
For us, the bug seems to lie in the update process itself and we are working on identifying the cause atm.
We will do our best to get this out asap, but i have not ETA yet.
To the best of our knowledge, it is caused by rolling out the update, so if you are planning to play through the demo you should be fine. 
Again, if you have experienced this and have anything you want to share, let us know below. It helps us :) 

Secondly, Autosave - we are working on this

Heard this one loud and clear, we are going to implement an autosave feature for the single player mode.
We already have a checkpoint feature in co-op so we are now in the midst of adapting a similar system into SP. Again, thanks to you all for the feedback on this one. 

Thirdly, the park is too dark in areas

We are paying attention to this. While the full game is both day and night, we want the night sections to be nerve racking and thrilling - but not frustrating. Essentially, the solution for us here is to take each area and assess how we can improve the overall lighting level. We can lift the darkness overall in the engine, however that would diminish some experiences where darkness is required.
Leave this with us, and I'll update you all in a future post with our plan.

Forthly! Dino Interactivity and AI

This one is a bit more varied but worth mentioning here. We are always working on improving our dino Ai and there are some behaviors we are looking to add, particularly with the herbivores. I won't give it away just yet, but some of these have been in the pipeline for a while as they are part of tourist mode. 
We are simply going to enable those behaviors in the Campaign mode too.

Discussions about the kind of interactions we want to see are important. We think about them all the time and if they make a good fit. 
Fun fact - all the dino have a built-in hunger system that we ultimately disabled after internal feedback was, they are too passive. The system was straight forward - If a carnivore is hungry, it will hunt you. If it is not, they will ignore you and go about their business. This worked great in our other mode, The Wilds, yet, in the Prehistoria mode, it meant you could encounter Reaper, one of our T-Rexes and he might just walk on by and the player is left wondering if the Ai was broken. It was a balancing nightmare.  

I share that story, just to let you know that all feedback is on the table if it improves the game experience. Being a small team has some advantages - we are adaptable. And making this game feel good to play and provide the experience we all hope for is really important to us.   

Fithly (im sure it's a word.) - Crouching and Stealth options.

This one had been a hot debate for us before the demo released. There has been a lot of Feeback on players want the ability to crouch and sneak. 
I won't over promise right now, however, rest assured, this is well on our radar. And we are looking at the full game experience and want to make sure that it will improve it overall before we pull the trigger :)

Sixthly -Ambient Noise - the park is too quiet.

This one is simple; we made our audio in some areas too quiet. We are going to adjust this. We are also looking into how to improve the ambient noise overall and will give this system an overhaul.
You guys had some awesome suggestions about this, so we will get on it.

Seventhly - Dino spawning

We've seen two main points here: Some dinos are showing up in places they shouldn't (like a stegosaur working in the information booth for example) and that the dinos are respawning when the player reloads the save and the player gets swarmed.

Both of these are being addressed. Again, thanks to all of you for pointing this one out.


So, I'll leave this here for now. Again, thanks to you all for being so supportive. Words can't express the gratitude we have for you. 

If you have any points you want to discuss, jump in the below and let us know

Thanks everyone

Tim

Flatrock Games

notes.title: Demo is live again!
notes.content:
Hey Prehistorians!

Tim here. 
As many of you may have seen, the Clawed demo has returned. We hope you will check it out and let us know what you think!

This past two weeks we addressees some nasty bugs that were affecting players on lower graphical settings and this has now been fixed. We also took a look at some feedback and reworked the latter half of the demo to improve the overall experience. Hudson had some animation improvements, and we made plenty of environmental improvements too. We have been working really hard to get this demo back online so hopefully the extra time spent will have been worth it.


We want your feedback and appreciate it.

So, already we have received a lot of kind messages, constructive feedback and general thoughts on our community discussions. This is great!
Your feedback really does help us tweak and polish this experience, learn valuable lessons, and get this game right before its release this year.
So, if you have anything you want to let us know, please do! Even if we have not replied to you directly yet, we are absolutely taking down every bit of feedback and listening.

So, while I have the floor here, let me address some of the issues right now :)

First of all, the Flashlight system. 

This one has been really interesting of us and in the spirit of transparency, I'm going to run you guys through our thoughts on the flashlight and what we're going to do next.

So, ironically, the original flashlight we had for a very long time was chest mounted and during internal testing, we received 2 main complaints: 
   1. that the flashlight didn't follow where people are aiming
   2. The characters aiming animations blocked the light during certain circumstances and would cause flickering when the player was sprinting as the arms would enter the light.

So, to address this, the weapon mounted flashlights were born. Now, we appreciate that this is maybe the most important tool in the game, so we want to get this right. We have received a lot of feedback about this and are looking into the best solution as the feedback on the light has varied quite a bit. However, we're hearing that the main issue is that the light is useless when you're not aiming (please correct me in the comments if you disagree)
In terms of gameplay tweaks, this is our biggest priority, and once the solution is implemented, we will be patching the demo.


Secondly, some players are getting a little lost.

So, this one is a little trickier, but we are moving on this. The feedback we are getting is that some players are not sure what they are supposed to do next.
So, here it is on our end. In Clawed, we are doing our best to keep the Hud down to a minimum as we really do want this experience to be immersive. We also want the players to be able to progress by using the environment and exploration to figure out the best way forward. Things like park map boards and notes were implemented to help guide the player through the park and towards their next objective.

Now, for some, this has been no issue and players have made their way to Peir A without struggling to much, but we are seeing some players are getting a little lost - especially because the game starts at night. So, while I don't have an exact solution I can share right now (I think each area needs its own solution anyway), I can say that we are going to add a park area map item that you can find and pickup. We already do this in the large dinosaur enclosures in the main game, so we are going to see if this will help with finding progression easier.

Again, if you have struggled with progression - lets chat about it. We are listening :)

Thirdly, Rain is too loud and can't be turned down.  
This one is simpler; the rain is too loud. We actually adjusted this prior to the demo releasing today, but we'll go back in and tune it some more. Also, the lack of a weather volume option was an oversight (by me actually if I need to point fingers). It will now get its own slider called "Weather Volume" in the audio volume section.

Forthly (is that a word?) Sprint toggle option is coming  
Another easy one, we are adding a sprint toggle option to the control settings tab. Controller players we hear you :)


Fifthly (lets go with it), the pistol will get a slight buff
While exploring is very important to survival, I've seen that not all players are locating weapons like the shotgun or AR. And so, Hudson's 9mm will receive a small buff (not too much) but enough to feel like you are not firing potatoes a charging raptor.

Sixthly, the inspect item bug makes me fall through the floor.
Now that I think about it, this should be number one on the list here, but I'm committed so here we are.
There is a bug when inspecting items in your inventory that can cause the player fall through the floor when they exit the inspection screen. This is a doozy, we are sorry we missed this one, but this will be fixed in the first round of patches. For now, maybe don't inspect your inventory items till the patch is up.

Seventhly, thanks for helping up make this game better. We want this to be a great experience, so your voice really helps us do that.

Okay, just know, we are watching everything and listening as much as we can. Constructive feedback is always welcome here, so keep it coming. We can't do everything that people ask, but I promise we will do our best.

Co-op? 

So, the plan for co-op is simple, once we get through the above-mentioned fixes and we feel the single player demo is in a happy place, we are going to open the co-op option up get all the feedback we can there too. Again, feedback really helps shape the game and getting it early is only going to help us make sure you enjoy the full game from the get-go.  We will keep you updated!   So, that's it for now. Again guys, thank you so much for the playing the demo. Let me know any thoughts you have on the discussion above or any other thoughts you may have :)  Have a great day!  Tim Flatrock Games


EDIT:

A NEW UPDATE IS NOW LIVE:

-Flashlight system has been reworked and is now mounted on the player.

-Pistol and Shotgun have received a small damage increase

-Main Gates now display the required key card on the control box to assist with knowing which key a gate needs.

We are hard a work addressing the remaining issues mentioned above :) Thanks to the community for the constructive feedback. We want this game to be a great time for you

notes.title: Demo update
notes.content:
HI Everyone, 

We wanted to take a moment to address the dinosaur size elephant in the room.

What happened to the demo?

Well, in the interest of transparency, we decided to pull it and here is why:

During the weeks leading up to the upcoming next fest we have been working around the clock to get this game ready for the show. It has been a really difficult and stressful time, but we didn't want to disappoint so many people that have supported the game since the announcement. 
So, we charged ahead and committed to putting the demo in for the festival. However, we encountered setback after setback and several were still being bug fixed all the way up to the final hours of our demo submission date.

We scrapped in, play tested it and submitted it.
But then we kept playing, and several issues popped up, one in particular was we found a glaring bug for players that played on lower graphical settings, and it made the game unplayable. 

For the next few hours we continued to test and get feedback, more bugs popped up - and it hit us hard - we made a mistake -This is not how we want to deliver this game for the people that have supported us. By trying not to delay the demo and disappoint our fans, we were in turn going to do just that - by releasing a demo that does not represent the quality of the experience we are working so hard to produce.

So, several hours after the demo went live, we decided to pull and withdraw from next week's Steam  Next Fest.

As many of us know, so many games get announced and then take forever to show up. We don't want that for Clawed, however, you all deserve a game to be excited for.
Exploring Prehistoria should be a thrilling, wonderful and terrifying experience that you can be immersed in without having glaring issues to detract from the experience.

We believe in being honest about our mistakes and we made a bad call here. Most of all, we are sorry to have disappointed you.

So, we are currently working on the polish and bugs we encountered and when the demo is ready (hopefully not too long) we will put it back up, with the issues address, co-op support and continue towards release later this year.

Tim
Flatrock Games

notes.title: Welcome to Prehistoria! Thank you for all the support!
notes.content:
Hello Dino lovers, Clawed community, T-rex trackers (we really need a community name)

Its Tim here from FDG and welcome to our first dev update for Clawed. There will be quite a few of these coming over the next few weeks and we are very excited to be able to share new info about Clawed.

But before all that, we want to extend a HUGE THANK YOU to all of you.
The amount of love and support we have received with this game has blown us away. 
Clawed has been a real passion project and the amount of emails, messages, social media clips and just love for this game has been completely unexpected. 
So again, thank you.

So i've got some info on the game i'm going to share here. I hope you enjoy, and yes if you have a question please ask. It takes a bit of time to get back, but we will. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45418326/8854e1860a82f47edff7e70074ccf80c2a94e5c7.png

Is the game real????
This one is a bit of a fun joke, but it actually amazed us just how many comments or messages we received wondering if the trailer is staged or a mockup of some kind. 
So, let me clear this all up now!
Everything in the trailer was taken from gameplay capture from a build of the game at the time.
In fact, the T-rex chasing the Tram was not even planned. That shot came by accident during the testing session. The planned shot was to get the Tram entering the Mosa Aquarium, but we had not realized the rex was nearby, and as soon as she saw Hudson, the chase was on.

The other notable thing in the trailer was that the bullets made little impact on the dinos when shot. 
Rest assured, this is not the case. Timing is a funny thing, as the long story short is - we had a bug with our hit reactions and did not have enough time to fix before our capture sessions.
So, as you will see in our next trailer, the reactions are physics based and are back in :)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45418326/fd6cc86d3fb911fcd61ce4ac79584f92c61304ba.png

What is Clawed like to play?
Well, simply put, this is an action/adventure mixed with Survival/Horror.
Its feels like RE2 remake in the way there are puzzles, inventory management and at times - it will make you sweat and shiver. However, this not a pure horror game, this game is scary because sometimes dinosaurs are scary. Being trapped in a dark tunnel as a raptor's call echoes down the hall will send shivers down your spine.
On the other side, there are time where you will be exploring Herbivore Haven - one of the largest enclosures in the game - and it's just fun to see the dinos out in the environment, doing what they do. 

Lastly, this in an open-world park. You will need to figure out how to reach certain areas, find the right keys or access cards and be equipped for what may be waiting for you. There are multiple routes through the park, so it's up to you to find them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45418326/ffb0e70626c86698b8716f59f01fcc79a0d82c78.png

There are multiple modes

In our current trailer, all the footage is from the main campaign (which can also be played in Co-op with up to 3 friends). However, there are two other modes that Clawed will also have at launch.

Tourist Mode

In tourist mode, you and up to 3 friends will be able to explore Prehistoria as an open zoo. You can take the tours, feed the brachiosaurus, buy souvenirs, and explore the park to your hearts content.
There is more to this mode, however, we will have an upcoming post about this mode with a lot more info.

The Wilds

In the Wilds, you and up to 3 friends will be deployed to an island where wild dinosaurs live and roam. Your goal will be to make money for your corporation. Explore the island, tranquilize dinos, recover artifacts, dino eggs and much more. Sell your discoveries back at your camp and buy new gear to help you bring in greater rewards. 
As with tourist mode, our plan is to do an upcoming blog post about this mode with a lot more info.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45418326/992121718ca44c065956d4dcfa5ad699ad5df82e.png

Are there going to be microtransactions??
No. 
Buy the game, it is yours. We are gamers ourselves, we get it, and any cosmetics, or updates will be free.

DLC?
There are currently no plans for a paid DLC, but a DLC model we feel is more respectful to the player base and would consider it IF we have an idea that we think respects the extra cost to the player. However, we really want the base game to feel like a complete experience, so it would have to be a large expansion for us to consider it. It would also be run by the community to ensure it would be of interest to Clawed players. Again, there are no plans for this right now.

Will there be a demo?

Yes. There will be. Soon.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45418326/f5eb9e3b60ee57a9125a68cf33487a6ca4fbb8d8.png

So, is that release window just a place holder?
No. No it is not.

As a studio, we are quite new. We have two games in development, and we tried to learn from each of them. Truthfully, our other game In The Dragon's Wake was maybe announced too early (Just being honest) and we learned from it. Maybe too well. So Clawed was kept to ourselves until we thought it was ready to be shown.
So, the current plan of Q2 is still in place, - its late Q2 for sure, but it is not a place holder. 
We are not ready yet to discuss the date until we are certain the game is ready. The last thing we want is announce a date and then delay it.
But rest assured the release date will be revealed soon :)
